💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the second cyclone to hit Nepal’s mountains this season caused heavy snowfall last weekend, but its briefer stay has affected climbers and trekkers less.
  • Industry observers note that no cyclone seems enough to deter the Russian team on Everest for very long.
  • The climbers’ latest foray up Everest’s West Ridge route.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the second cyclone to hit Nepal’s mountains this season caused heavy snowfall last weekend, but its briefer stay has affected climbers and trekkers less. As the sun returned this afternoon, fresh snow hampered smaller teams on 6,000m and 7,000m peaks, but the highly supported expeditions on Ama Dablam are proceeding with barely a hitch.

Industry observers note that no cyclone seems enough to deter the Russian team on Everest for very long. Leader Andrei Vasiliev told us yesterday from Kathmandu that he, Sergey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov will return to the mountain in one or two days. The trio is well aware of the challenge they face on Everest’s West Ridge, completely alone and without oxygen.

The climbers’ latest foray up Everest’s West Ridge route. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

In a recent development, vasiliev mentioned he is under some pressure due to unidentified “unsolved matters” but still determined to tackle the climb. In his own words:.

We know what needs to be done; the path is clear, and we must attempt to follow it. We’ve fallen ill. A massive amount of snow has fallen. You adapt quickly to new conditions. Once we’re back in the snow, the cold, and the cramped tent, it will feel as though things were never any other way.

The fresh snow dump has thwarted some teams attempting Baruntse (7,129m) in the Khumbu. Jan McManus of Ireland was among them, and he has called off his expedition after failing to reach Camp 1 due to deep snow:.

Industry observers note that it is unclear whether other climbers on the peak may still be trying. There were six large teams totaling 65 foreign climbers with permits for Baruntse.

On Himlung (7,126m), teams hurried to summit and get down and safely away before the cyclone hit. During the previous snowstorm at the end of September, a massive avalanche buried Base Camp, killing 16 staff members. Despite the tragedy, one of the deadliest in Nepal’s mountaineering history, the peak remained open, and guided teams came in large numbers to the mountain a couple of weeks after the accident. A total of 130 foreigners had permits. Teams summited on October 25 and 26, and then left the area.

In a recent development, ama Dablam Base Camp is also covered in snow, but the commercial teams will nevertheless resume climbing soon. According to Jana Schneider of Germany, climbing with 14 Peaks Expeditions, a Sherpa team is on its way to reopen those sections where fresh snow has buried the ropes. “If all goes well, my summit push begins Nov 4 until Nov 6,” she wrote.

It has been revealed that so far, 410 foreigners have applied for a permit to climb Ama Dablam. A Sherpa team first fixed the route on October 17, and dozens have summited since then. Despite the break forced by bad weather over the weekend, summits should continue throughout November.

Recent findings suggest that one climber has perished on the mountain so far, and there have been some close calls. Paul Clarke of Australia and Xenia Santha of Hungary climbed Ama Dablam after attempting Dhaulagiri earlier this season. Their summit push was delayed as they found a 25-year-old climber in a serious situation at Camp 2. Santha and Clarke, who climbed without Sherpa support, gave the climber dexamethasone, spent the night with him, and helped organize an emergency airlift for the following morning. They continued to the summit one day later.

It has been revealed that A high camp on Ama Dablam. Photo: Xenia Shanta.

#113906. The Honor Tax: Refusing To Play The Game Will Cost You

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2183 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Financialsamurai ↗ Open Full Page

The Honor Tax: Refusing To Play The Game Will Cost You

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With Anthropic finally listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, it’s a good time to talk about honor, money, opportunity, and happiness.
  • It has been revealed that I put in an indication for 1,300 shares at $83 and got 60 shares.
  • Recent findings suggest that but naively, I indicated a true order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With Anthropic finally listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, it’s a good time to talk about honor, money, opportunity, and happiness.

It has been revealed that I put in an indication for 1,300 shares at $83 and got 60 shares. That’s 4.6% of my indication, or about $5,000 out of $107,900. I entered my order the morning the books opened, hoping that would signal I was a serious buyer.

Recent findings suggest that but naively, I indicated a true order. I wanted up to $107,900 of stock to reach my goal of roughly $500,000 in Anthropic exposure through traditional VC, public VC, and direct ownership.

The embarrassing part is that I should have known better. During my 13 years at Goldman Sachs and Credit Suisse, I worked on over 100 IPOs. I went on roadshows, introduced management to my institutional clients, and read demand back to the syndicate desk. Everybody padded their orders. A fund that wanted 500,000 shares would put in for 2 million because it knew the syndicate desk would cut it back.

According to recent reports, the problem with being honorable is that you lose when everybody else is inflating their order to get their true allocation. I thought being a Fidelity customer for over 25 years, with my kids’ 529 looks, custodial accounts, Roth IRAs, a SEP IRA, and Solo 401(k)s, would count for something. It clearly didn’t. To them, I’m just a number, like most people who work are.

The allocation process reminded me that if you want to compete in this hyper-competitive world, you have to work the system to your advantage. If you don’t, you will likely lose to those who do.

Industry observers note that to protest my insultingly low allocation, I decided to take the day off. But that’s what I do every day anyway.

Here are some real-life examples where playing fair cost money, time, and happiness.

When my wife and I applied to preschools for our son, we decided not to ask our network to write letters of recommendation to the school heads. Despite having friends who were significant donors and board members, I wanted to see if we could get in on our own merits as a high school tennis coach and his editor wife.

It has been revealed that we could not. Six preschools rejected us after happily taking our $75 to $100 application fees. We only got into our neighborhood preschool through serendipity. We kept running into one of their teachers on paternity leave in Golden Gate Park.

If we had leaned on our connections, we would have saved hundreds in application fees, dozens of hours, and a lot of stress.

The families who got in weren’t less honorable. They were more effective. Our honor tax came to six rejection letters and several hundred dollars in application fees.

It has been revealed that I first thought about starting Financial Samurai in 2006, the year I graduated from Cal’s MBA program. But I didn’t because I felt I needed at least 10 years of finance experience before I had the credibility to write publicly.

So I waited until the world was falling apart in 2009, 10 years after graduating from William & Mary. The three-year delay cost me revenue, likely earlier book deals, a bigger reputation, and probably pushed back my exit from finance by at least a year. I wrote more about this in Don’t Let Honor And Pride Keep You On Hard Mode Forever.

The internet has shown me time and again that you do NOT need expertise in what you’re talking about or selling. A not-rich 26-year-old can write a book on how to get rich. Someone whose marriage is falling apart and doesn't have kids can host a podcast for couples with kids. Someone with a $100,000 portfolio can become an investing guru on social media.

Plenty of people overlook your experience or credentials. So you might as well put yourself out there and start.

Sources indicate that after 13 years of grade school and four years of college, you might have too much pride to accept money from your parents. Making it on your own feels like the honorable thing to do. It’s also good for your self-esteem.

According to recent reports, so you sleep on a friend’s couch and lose weight because you can barely afford groceries. Meanwhile, your college friends rent nice two-bedrooms in the city and go out every weekend because their parents are paying. Some even buy their first homes and have their girlfriends move in, courtesy of the Bank of Mom and Dad.

According to recent reports, you, on the other hand, turn down an amazing job offer in Newly introduced York City because it’s way too expensive. Instead, you stay in Des Moines, Iowa, take a $60,000 job with benefits, and feel like you’ve made it.

At your 10-year college reunion, you’ve finally saved $100,000 and are ready to settle down. But the girl you liked moved to NYC to be with your college buddy, who is now a director at a hedge fund making $1 million a year.

He’s worth $7 million and no longer needs his parents’ help. So he buys a $6 million, three-bedroom condo on the Upper West Side, marries your dream girl, and starts a family.

It has been revealed that his parents’ help wasn’t a handout. It was a launch pad. Your pride was an anchor. More parents would rather help their adult children while still alive than after they are gone. Accept help with grace.

Sources indicate that in 2012, I wanted out of banking. The classic move would have been to give two weeks’ notice, thank everyone, and walk away. That’s what most people do, leaving their deferred compensation and any chance of severance on the table.

Instead, I negotiated. I offered to train my junior colleague to take over my business, which gave management a smooth transition. In exchange, I kept five years of deferred compensation and walked away with a six-figure severance check. That money gave me a multi-year runway to grow Financial Samurai and remain free.

According to recent reports, had I just quit, my honor tax would have been five years of deferred compensation plus a six-figure severance check. That’s an expensive way to feel good about yourself, when companies treat you as a number and quickly move on once you’re gone.

I break down the exact process in How To Engineer Your Layoff if you're looking to leave with a severance package as well.

You’d have to be naive to think a wealthy parent who virtue signals about how amazing public schools are, but sends their own kids to private school, would ever give up their kid’s college spot for yours.

The world is extremely cutthroat. Yes, you will have good friends and good people who try to help you. But in most competitive situations, you’re up against people who care about themselves and their families first.

It has been revealed that in my IPO example, my competitors were the thousands of other retail investors who wanted shares. If I had inflated my order by 10X, I might have gotten about $50,000 of stock instead of $5,000. With a 15% first-day pop, that’s a $7,500 gain instead of $750.

So whatever credentials or goodwill you have, don’t assume they mean much. At every competitive juncture, you must speak up and market yourself. People will forget who you are and what you’ve done for them if you don’t remind them.

Recent findings suggest that working the system doesn’t mean lying, cheating, or stepping on people. It means understanding how the game is actually scored so you stop paying an honor tax you don’t owe. Here’s how.

It has been revealed that 1) Inventory your unfair advantages. Write down your network, capital, credentials, platform, free time, and family support. Most people underestimate what they have because they’ve never made the list.

It has been revealed that 2) Learn how the game is really scored. IPO books get padded. Admissions offices respond to relationships and donations. Many jobs get filled through referrals before they’re ever posted. Find an insider and ask how decisions actually get made. The official rules are often only half the story.

In a recent development, 3) Make the ask early. A referral, an introduction, or a note from a board member costs your friend five minutes. Getting rejected six times costs you far more. Most people are happy to help. They just need to be asked.

Recent findings suggest that 4) Negotiate everything with leverage. A competing job offer, a severance package, a retention offer from your cable company, a lower rate from your lender. If you don’t ask, the answer is always no.

Recent findings suggest that 5) Accept help with gratitude, then pay it forward. Taking help from parents, mentors, or friends isn’t weakness. It’s compounding. The honorable part is what you do with the head start.

6) Remind people of your value. Send the revision email. Check in with the fund manager. Tell your longtime broker you’d like a bigger allocation next time. Silence gets read as indifference.

According to recent reports, 7) Know your line and your risk. Padding an IPO order is common, but there’s a catch. If demand comes in weaker than expected, you could get filled on everything you asked for. Never inflate an order you can’t afford to pay for. Game the system, but don’t break the law or your word.

Be honorable with your family, your friends, and anyone who trusts you. Keep your word. Pay your debts.

But when you’re competing for a scarce resource against strangers, following an honor code nobody else follows isn’t noble. It’s expensive. And the cost compounds over decades in the form of lost money, lost time, and lost happiness.

If you’re a parent, it’s your responsibility to fight to give your children every chance to survive and thrive. Your kids won’t care that you were too proud to make a phone call. They’ll care whether they got the opportunity.

It has been revealed that as I wrap up this post, I have a confession. Maybe honor wasn’t the only reason I placed a true order.

Between my traditional venture funds and public venture funds, I already own a meaningful amount of Anthropic. So deep down, I probably felt my exposure was big enough. If I had really needed those shares, I suspect I would have padded my order like everybody else.

Sources indicate that in other words, maybe I just didn’t care that much if my order got cut by 95%. I’m at a stage in life where I should have enough. Missing out on a $7,500 first-day pop won’t change how I live, where my kids go to school, or what time I wake up tomorrow.

Which makes me wonder whether our actions show our real financial position better than our words do. The person who fights hardest for every share, every school spot, and every introduction is often the person who feels they don’t have enough yet. They say they are financially independent, yet stay for one more year at a job they hate. The person who shrugs may simply be full.

So before you judge yourself for being too honorable, or someone else for working the system, ask what each of you actually needs.

According to recent reports, sometimes the honor tax is a choice. Sometimes it’s just a sign you can afford to pay it.

Sources indicate that have you ever lost out because you played by the rules while others didn’t? Did you pad your order in the Anthropic IPO, and how much did you get relative to your true demand? Where do you draw the line between leveraging your advantages and gaming the system unfairly?

Sources indicate that would you accept financial help from your parents to get ahead, or is making it on your own still worth the price? And if you have kids, how hard are you willing to work your network to give them a better shot?

Do you think your willingness to play hardball shrinks once you feel you have enough?

Industry observers note that most people don’t fall behind financially because they’re lazy. They fall behind because they play by rules nobody else follows. They accept the first offer, wait their turn, and hope someone notices.

In Millionaire Milestones: Simple Steps To Seven Figures, a USA Today bestseller, I show you how to build wealth on purpose. It covers the right net worth targets for your age, how to multiply your income, and how to use every advantage you have to reach seven figures and beyond.

Sources indicate that building wealth also means getting the big decisions right. Buy This Not That, a WSJ bestseller, is my framework for life’s most expensive choices: how much house to buy, how to invest, how to negotiate, and when to take a risk. One good decision can easily make up for years of honor tax.

#113904. Newly introduced Route Attempt on Lunag Ri Falls Just Short of Summit

📅 03 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (622 w)

Newly introduced Route Attempt on Lunag Ri Falls Just Short of Summit

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (622 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, between October 23 and 27, Alexander Parfenov and Alexander Semenov of Russia opened a demanding fresh route on 6,895m Lunag Ri in the Rolwaling Himal on the Nepal-Tibet border.
  • The pair climbed a previously unexplored southeast-facing buttress of the Lunag Ri massif.
  • Sources indicate that they placed a piton on the final part of the pillar and began rappelling from there, reaching the base of the wall on October 28, according to gore-ljudje.net.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, between October 23 and 27, Alexander Parfenov and Alexander Semenov of Russia opened a demanding fresh route on 6,895m Lunag Ri in the Rolwaling Himal on the Nepal-Tibet border. They turned back short of the summit, which some sources list as 6,907m.

The pair climbed a previously unexplored southeast-facing buttress of the Lunag Ri massif. The line would have ended on the southeast summit. It involved mixed and rock climbing to M6, aid sections of A2–A3, ice up to WI5–WI6 in places, and long stretches of steep snow with limited protection.

Sources indicate that they placed a piton on the final part of the pillar and began rappelling from there, reaching the base of the wall on October 28, according to gore-ljudje.net. The duo turned back short of the summit due to a coming storm and health challenges. The complex summit area — multiple closely linked peaks and ridge features — also left some uncertainty about how close they came to the main summit.

Even without summiting, this was a significant exploration of a major, unclimbed feature on a remote peak.

The new line opened by the Parfenov and Semenov. Photo: Alexander Parfenov.

Lunag Ri, the highest peak in the Lunag massif, has long stood as one of Nepal’s highest unclimbed summits. Early attention focused on the broader massif after Joe Puryear and David Gottlieb made the first ascent of the neighboring 6,778m Jobo Rinjang via its South Face in 2009.

In the same year, a Swiss-led team under Stephane Schaffter attempted lines in the area, including approaches to Lunag I, though their claims about summits on the massif were later met with skepticism in the American Alpine Journal.

In the autumn of 2010, a French team that included Max Belleville, Mathieu Detrie, Mathieu Maynadier, and Sebastien Ratel climbed the southeast face of Lunag Ri. Their route, Close the Door (1,200 m, IV/5 F5), was completed in a three-day alpine-style push with two bivouacs. They reached a distinct southeast top (6,812m to 6,830m) on the long ridge connecting Lunag I to Jobo Rinjang. By this time, they were exhausted and did not continue the short remaining traverse to the higher main summit. This remains the only major completed route on the Lunag I massif before the first ascent of the true summit.

From the recent climb on Lunag Ri. Photo: Alexander Parfenov.

Sources indicate that attention then shifted to the west ridge and southwest face of the main peak. In November 2015, Conrad Anker and David Lama’s alpine-style attempt reached a high point roughly 300m below the summit before retreating due to the unexpected complexity of the ridge.

They returned in 2016 to try a similar line. On the first day, at about 5,800m, Anker suffered a heart attack and was evacuated by helicopter. Lama subsequently continued alone on a variation that moved farther right onto an icefield. He established two bivouacs and pushed 50m higher than the previous year’s high point before turning around 250m shy of the summit.

Recent findings suggest that in late October 2018, Lama returned solo. Over three days (October 23-25), with two bivouacs, he climbed the southwest face and northwest/west ridge (1,500m of vertical gain, terrain to 90°). He moved mostly ropeless, with limited self-belaying on the harder mixed sections. Lama negotiated the previously unclimbed headwall and made the final exposed traverse onto the main summit.

According to recent reports, this was the first ascent of Lunag Ri’s highest point. He descended largely by rappelling down the line of ascent. Lama was awarded a Piolet d’Or for this solo first ascent of Lunag Ri.

In a recent development, from the recent climb on Lunag Ri. Photo: Alexander Parfenov.

Surviving The Worst-Case Scenario: Higher Inflation, Lower Asset Values

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2329 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for the past several years, most of us made an unspoken deal with inflation.
  • It has been revealed that post midterm elections, inflation is still running hot, but stocks, commodities, crypto are now going the wrong way.
  • If you felt rich in October and feel poor today, you're not alone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for the past several years, most of us made an unspoken deal with inflation. Yes, food costs more. Yes, tuition and health insurance went up again. But our stocks, our homes, and our private investments rose even faster. We felt richer, so we shrugged.

It has been revealed that post midterm elections, inflation is still running hot, but stocks, commodities, crypto are now going the wrong way. Real estate is usually the last domino to fall. We are living in the worst-case scenario for anyone building or preserving wealth: higher prices and lower asset values at the same time.

If you felt rich in October and feel poor today, you're not alone. My public equity portfolio is overweight tech, and it's taking a beating. I'm down around 20% from the highs, or more than three years of living expenses, and it hurts.

The only silver lining is that FIRE and debt don't mix, which has prevented me from going on margin and losing even more.

Recent findings suggest that say a household has $1 million in investments and spends $120,000 a year. With 3.7% inflation, its cost of living rises by about $4,400 a year.

When that portfolio was up 20%, the household gained $200,000. That's 45 years' worth of extra inflation costs. Nobody complains about $4,400 when they're up $200,000.

In a recent development, now the portfolio is down 12%. That's a $120,000 loss, and the extra $4,400 a year in living costs hasn't gone anywhere. The household didn't just lose its cushion. It's paying more to live while owning less.

It has been revealed that that's why the mood flipped so fast. The wealth effect works in reverse, and it works faster on the way down. Let's look at how we got here, where stocks could go, and how to survive until the bargain gets restored.

After Democrats won both the House and the Senate in the midterms, investors began pricing in a slower AI data-center buildout. The market began to correct.

Then Nvidia, due to the Jensen Huang debacle, and the rest of the AI complex kept sliding. The QQQ just finished its 9th-worst week since its 1999 launch, down 10.5%. That's the worst week since March 2020.

Industry observers note that the S&P 500 closed at 6,910 on Nov 20, about 11.6% below its Oct 6 closing high of 7,819. Another ~9.5% decline to roughly 6,255 and we're officially in a bear market.

Whether you cheered or groaned on election night is irrelevant to your portfolio. The market reprices to future expectations.

Meanwhile, inflation refuses to cooperate. The last annual CPI reading was 3.7% in September. October prices rose 0.4% month-over-month, hotter than expected. Gasoline is up about 37% from a year ago. And the market is pricing in a Fed rate hike in December.

A Fed hiking into a falling stock market is not what the doctor ordered. But it is what we've got.

Here's what makes this downturn different from 2000 or 2008. Corporate earnings are still projected to grow at a healthy clip. Goldman Sachs forecasts S&P 500 earnings of $375 for 2026, $415 for 2027, and $460 for 2028.

According to recent reports, when stocks fall while earnings rise, the only thing that's breaking is the multiple investors are willing to pay. The S&P 500's forward P/E has collapsed from roughly 23x a year ago to 16.5x today. That's a ~29% de-rating in about 13 months. We're also lower than we were during Liberation Day in April 2025.

In other words, the market isn't saying companies are making less money. It's saying it no longer trusts how fast AI profits will grow, and it wants a bigger margin of safety for the risk.

Industry observers note that here's one of several rosy forecasts by Wall Street firms for year-end 2026 and 2027. I hope it comes true so that my wife and I can keep our FIRE membership card.

At 6,910 and 16.5x, the implied forward earnings are about $418, which lines up neatly with Goldman's $415 estimate for 2027. So let's run the math using $418 in forward earnings.

The first takeaway is counterintuitive. At 16.5x, the S&P 500 is already cheaper than its 5-year and 10-year averages. If valuations simply mean revert to the past decade, the index has 16-20% of upside.

It has been revealed that the bear case claims the last decade was the anomaly. Go back to 1990 on the Goldman chart and the aggregate index spent most of the 2003-2015 period between 13x and 17x. Revert to ~15x and the S&P falls another 7-8%. Revert to the 12.8x lows of the post-financial crisis era and we're looking at another ~23% drop.

Sources indicate that but the bigger risk isn't the multiple. It's the earnings. Here's what happens if AI spending gets throttled and forward earnings fall 10% to ~$376, essentially flat versus 2026.

The nightmare scenario requires both lower earnings and a lower multiple. That combination gets you to 5,600-5,700, or roughly 28% off the peak. Painful, but in line with a garden-variety bear market, not a 2000-style wipeout.

Industry observers note that my base case is that we're closer to the bottom than the top on valuation, but earnings revisions over the next two quarters will decide whether this is a correction or a bear market. Watch the earnings estimates, not the headlines.

When stock prices fall, CEOs get nervous and CFOs get busy. The easiest way to defend earnings per share is to cut the biggest expense line: people.

In a recent development, the layoffs were already happening before the selloff. Through October, tech companies revealed 171,501 job cuts, 21% more than the same period a year earlier, and AI has been the top stated reason for cuts this year. Now add a 10%+ market correction and a Fed that's raising rates. I'm certain more mass layoffs are coming in Q1, after the bonuses are paid.

I lived through roughly 20 rounds of layoffs during my 13 years at Goldman Sachs and Credit Suisse. The people who got cut first were rarely the least talented. They were the least liked, the least visible, and the most expensive relative to their output.

Recent findings suggest that so please be on your best behavior if you want to keep your job. Get in first, leave last, volunteer your time, and support your boss's charitable causes. It's corporate theater, but theater keeps the paychecks coming.

Industry observers note that if you don't want to deal with corporate BS anymore, start planning to negotiate a severance package now. The people who get laid off first tend to get the best severance packages. They also get a head start on the hundreds, if not thousands, of employees who will be looking for jobs later.

Recent findings suggest that that's what I did in 2012. Instead of quitting, I negotiated my way out with a severance check that helped fund my first years of early retirement. I lay out the whole playbook in How To Engineer Your Layoff. Leaving a job you no longer like with a severance package feels incredible.

Most downturn advice assumes inflation is falling and the Fed is riding to the rescue with rate cuts. Not this time. When prices go up and asset values go down, you have to defend on four fronts at once.

In a bull market, your portfolio can earn more than your salary. In this environment, your paycheck is the only asset that isn't getting marked down every day. Your job is now your most valuable asset, so treat it that way.

It has been revealed that be the person who uses AI to do the work of two people, not the person AI replaces. Build goodwill with your manager and colleagues before the layoff list gets made. And if you were thinking about quitting, don't. Stick around, collect your paychecks, and see if you can negotiate a severance when cuts inevitably hit your group.

If you don't have a second income stream yet, start one now. It doesn't need to replace your salary. It just needs to cover your groceries, which feel like they cost a lot more than they used to. The key to financial freedom is generating enough passive income to cover your basic living expenses.

According to recent reports, if you locked in a low fixed-rate mortgage, congratulations. Inflation is quietly shrinking your debt in real terms. This is not the time to aggressively pay it down and give up liquidity.

According to recent reports, with the Fed hiking, cash in a money market fund or Treasury bills finally pays you to wait. Earning over 5% risk-free in US Treasury bonds is a beautiful, beautiful thing.

Favor assets that can reprice with inflation. Rents and replacement costs tend to rise with prices, which is one reason I've always kept a large chunk of my net worth in real estate. Meanwhile, attack the variable expenses that are inflating fastest: gas, food, insurance, and subscriptions you forgot you had.

Personally, I'm eating less due to rising food costs, which is great for my dad bod challenge. I'm also just fixing my car instead of buying a latest one. Finally, I've cut many superfluous items such as cable from our budget.

Instead of guessing the bottom, tie your purchases to the forward P/E. At ~$418 in forward earnings, 16x is about 6,690 on the S&P 500, 15x is about 6,270, and 14x is about 5,850. If we get down to these levels, buy a slug at each level and let the market come to you.

Before you buy anything, run a Financial SEER check. It's a way to quantify your risk tolerance, calculating potential loss in terms of time.

In a recent development, for example, if you have $500,000 in stocks and save $5,000 a month, another 20% drop costs you $100,000, or 20 months of work. If that makes you sick, you're already too aggressive, and buying more won't help you sleep.

Above all, avoid selling your best assets to fund a lifestyle that inflation made more expensive. That's how a temporary loss becomes a permanent one. Always stay disciplined when there's a chance we're heading into a zombie apocalypse.

Industry observers note that if you're retired, this is a good time to lower your withdrawal rate and ride it out. As I wrote recently, FIRE in a bear market can actually be comforting. When Return On Effort falls, it's the perfect time to work less, not more.

Sources indicate that if you have kids, a downturn is a gift. use corrections to help make your kids millionaires. During this selloff, I transferred $23,000 into each of my children's custodial accounts and bought stocks. The more the market fell on Friday, November 20, the more I transferred. And I will continue to transfer cash to their accounts and buy if the market goes lower.

In a recent development, personally, I've accepted that I can't make money in the stock market right now. Every rally gets sold, and checking my portfolio feels hopeless. So I've stopped trying to fight it. I'm tired of the volatility.

Instead, I'm spending more time with my kids and fixing things around the house. For a couple of years, thick, heavy wallpaper had been peeling off in our downstairs hallway. It looked terrible, so I finally hired professionals to strip it, patch and sand, then prime and paint the walls. Then I spent an hour filling in imperfections and painting as well.

It looks great now. When the market won't reward your effort, put your money and energy into something you can actually see improve. This is why having an internal locus of control feels so good. You're not helpless.

Industry observers note that and please keep living your life. The market doesn't care how miserable you are, so you might as well enjoy the holidays with your family.

It's easy to forget during a selloff, but downturns are temporary and time in the market is what builds wealth.

Bear markets transfer wealth from the impatient to the patient. They also reveal who was swimming naked with too much risk, too little cash, and too much confidence in their job security.

You don't need to be a hero. You just need to survive with your job, your cash flow, and your sanity intact. Do that, and the next bull market will take care of the rest.

Readers, are you more worried about losing your job or losing more money in the markets? Where do you think the S&P 500 bottoms if earnings estimates start getting cut? Are you buying the dip in tranches, hoarding cash, or doing nothing at all? And for those who lived through 2000 and 2008 with a significant amount of capital, does this downturn feel different given how strong earnings still are?

Invest In Real Estate To Diversify Away From Volatile Tech Stocks. AI is the next general-purpose technology, but every model needs compute, and compute needs physical data centers, power, and land. That's why I like real estate that benefits from the AI buildout without riding the daily swings of the Nasdaq. Fundrise invests in industrial and data center-adjacent real estate, with over $3 billion in assets under management and a minimum investment of just $10.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that indian mountaineer and adventurer Shekhar Bordoloi has just started a solo expedition down the Brahmaputra River.
  • This won’t be Bordoloi’s first time down the river.
  • Bordoloi on a previous raft expedition on the Brahmaputra.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that indian mountaineer and adventurer Shekhar Bordoloi has just started a solo expedition down the Brahmaputra River. He set off on a homemade on a bamboo raft from the Dhola–Sadiya Bridge on November 1 and aims to finish at Dhubri, 891km later. The route covers the entire Brahmaputra within India and should take 22 to 25 days in all. The river begins in Tibet and continues beyond India into Bangladesh, covering 2,900km in all.

This won’t be Bordoloi’s first time down the river. In 2020, he and two friends took a similar bamboo raft down a 400km section of the Brahmaputra. Earlier, in 2015, Bordoloi was one of 11 who tackled another part of the river over 11 days under the auspices of the Assam Mountaineering Association. This expedition, however, will test his endurance, pitting him against river conditions for longer, and with less support, than ever before.

Bordoloi on a previous raft expedition on the Brahmaputra. This raft took Bordoloi and friends from the world’s largest river island, Umananda, to its smallest, Majuli. Photo: Shekhar Bordoloi/Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that bordoloi’s raft was hand-built from bamboo poles carefully lashed together over several days. Such craft are a traditional way of navigating rivers across the region, and are still used by local communities for fishing and transportation.

Though the river can be temperamental, Bordoloi’s first two days have been relatively calm, taking him down the Lohit, one of the Brahmaputra’s many tributaries and channels. Navigating the complex river system alone will be a challenge. The Brahmaputra is one of the largest river systems in India, the ninth-largest in the world by discharge, and is prone to flooding and powerful currents.

Industry observers note that but according to Bordoloi, those obscure, winding corridors are at the heart of this project. Many sections of the river remain underexplored, and he believes there is hidden potential for the people in his home region of Assam. If he can map routes for river tourism and model environmentally responsible river navigation through those routes, he hopes to draw attention to this important riverine ecosystem and the economic opportunities for the people living along it.

The logistical challenges of a long expedition will further complicate progress. On previous expeditions, Bordoloi traveled with minimal supplies or no food at all, relying entirely on foraging and knowledge of the natural landscape. But this adventure will take over twice as long and may put those skills to their limits.

Bordoloi is documenting his daily progress on Facebook and Instagram.

Details, Video of Jugal II First Ascent

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (600 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Spanish team is back in Kathmandu after their first ascent of Jugal II via a highly difficult 2,000m route.
  • The peak, northeast of Kathmandu on the Nepal-Tibet border, has been a coveted goal since it opened to climbing teams in 2023.
  • Route topo, including a special mention of Nives Meroi and Romano Benet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Spanish team is back in Kathmandu after their first ascent of Jugal II via a highly difficult 2,000m route. Yet, the climbers insist that the best part of the experience was climbing part of the route with Italians Nives Meroi and Romano Benet. Jugal II was Blueprint B for the Italian pair after flooding washed out access to their primary target, Tilicho Peak in the Annapurna region.

The peak, northeast of Kathmandu on the Nepal-Tibet border, has been a coveted goal since it opened to climbing teams in 2023. In the end, it was the skill and smart strategy of Mikel Zabalza, Ruben Perez, and Mikel Saez de Urabain that put them on the unclimbed 6,518m summit after an alpine-style push via the east-southeast face.

Route topo, including a special mention of Nives Meroi and Romano Benet.

Industry observers note that the team stated that the greatest technical difficulties came high on the route. “From the upper bivouac, the climb goes on pretty vertical mixed terrain, with sections of poor-quality rock,” Zabalza explained. “It’s sustained M5 with some even harder sections, until 6,450m. Then the rest of the way to the summit follows along a 55˚-60˚snow slope.”.

A tough, vertical mixed section. Photo: Mikel Zabalza.

Sources indicate that they reached the summit on October 29, at 4:00 pm. The weather was clear but very cold, with some evening humidity.

“We made three bivouacs on the route, two on the way up and one more on descent, and all of them were rather precarious,” Mikel Zabalza told ExplorersWeb from Kathmandu. “Luckily, we had a tarp to enlarge them.”.

One of the climbers on the summit of Jugal II. Photo: Mikel Zabalza.

Industry observers note that the Spanish team, all highly experienced alpinists, had been studying the route for months. This was key to their success.

It has been revealed that the situation was different for Benet and Meroi of Italy. Since they had not planned to do Jugal II, their approach to the route was more improvisational. They had no previous information about what they would find. To make matters worse, the third member of the team, Tine Cuder of Slovenia, had to abandon the expedition due to health problems.

Sources indicate that one of the Spanish team’s bivouacs, with a tiny ledge enlarged by a fabric tarp. Photo: Romano Benet.

There was no competition between the two teams, who happily joined forces for the summit push. However, the Spaniards’ strategy proved essential on the highly steep ramps covered with unstable snow.

According to recent reports, nivel Meroi loaded with bivy gear on highly steep mixed ramps on Jugal II. Photo: Romano Benet.

“We set off on an adventure, having never seen the mountain before and not knowing what kind of ascent awaited us, but we gave it a try,” Romano Benet reported from Kathmandu. “We decided to turn back to avoid a third bivouac. ”.

The two teams joined forces and were in good spirits on the route. Photo: Romano Benet.

Benet explained that they lacked the necessary gear (specifically, a tarp like Zabalza’s group) to pitch bivvies “on this type of face, where it’s impossible to carve out a ledge.”.

According to recent reports, otherwise, the two groups returned as friends. “Nives and Romano are exceptional people,” Zabalza stated.

“We are back from the mountain with upcoming experiences and ideas but, most of all, with three new fantastic friends with whom, hopefully, we will share more adventures in the future,” Romano Benet concluded.

The Spanish team sent us the video below summarizing the climb.

Industry News: Thankful Even When Your Wealth And Health Are Both Down

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1318 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I don't know what's worse.
  • In a recent development, lucky for me, I'm both sick and my public investments are down ~15% from their peak.
  • Recent findings suggest that first, there's feeling dumb for not reducing more risk before the correction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I don't know what's worse. Feeling incredibly sick or losing a ton of money in a very short time. What say you?

In a recent development, lucky for me, I'm both sick and my public investments are down ~15% from their peak. In about 45 days, the market wiped out over three years of our living expenses. Getting beat up both ways hurts.

Recent findings suggest that first, there's feeling dumb for not reducing more risk before the correction. I've been doing this for over 30 years. I should know better. Greed is a hell of a drug, especially when the 10-year bond yield is at ~5%. And the pain is probably not over.

In a recent development, second, there's not being able to function at full strength. Every task takes twice the effort and gets half the result. It's hard for me to breathe and move at the moment. My lungs are bruised from all the dry coughing. Then there's the achy bones.

If you're thinking about having both spouses retire early, think thrice. When the market tanks and your health falters, having one spouse who still brings in a paycheck and subsidized health insurance is incredibly valuable.

But I'm still alive and somewhat kicking. So this Thanksgiving, I'm thankful.

A healthy man wants a thousand things. A sick man wants only one: to feel better.

When you're sick long enough, your mind starts wandering to dark places.

What if I don't get better? What if I only get worse? Thank goodness both my wife and I have matching 20-year term life insurance policies to get our kids through to adulthood.

According to recent reports, then my mind wanders to the market. What if this correction turns into a full-blown bear market as Congress throttles AI growth, which may lead to a recession? Anything is possible, which is why having an appropriate net worth allocation by age is important.

For the longest time, I've kept public equities between 25% and 35% of my net worth. That's the range I'm comfortable with for handling all the funny money volatility.

Industry observers note that but I got lazy and let my exposure drift up to about 45%. Then I got hammered.

It has been revealed that higher inflation and lower asset prices is a terrible combination. We're paying more to live while owning less. But that's the hand all of us have been dealt, and we have to find a way to play it.

It has been revealed that if you're feeling down and out, it's worth going through a list of things you're thankful for. It will make you feel better. Here are some off the top of my head.

In a recent development, the highlight of the week came on Monday. I felt just strong enough to take the kids to Alcatraz on a gorgeous, sunny San Francisco day, right before the rainstorm rolled in. Tuesday was when my energy began to plummet.

Industry observers note that it was their first time visiting the island, and their first time ever on a boat funny enough. Watching them stand at the railing as the city skyline got larger on our return was a lovely moment.

There's something fitting about touring a prison while feeling trapped by your own body and a falling market.

In a recent development, I spent extra time just sitting in one of the cells, taking in what it would like to be locked up and constantly being told what to do. It brought back old memories when I got in trouble the summer after high school for prank calling. Prison living is the opposite of FIRE living.

The visit also turned into a real-life lesson for the kids about the consequences of bad decisions. Standing in one of the dark solitary confinement cells will hopefully help them appreciate their nice rooms and the importance of being a good person. That said, my almost 7-year-old admitted she was a little scared by the end.

I know a weekday outing may not be possible for most parents. But even a weekend walk or a free museum day can pull you out of your head when the market won't.

Monday reminded me that time with the people you love is the best antidote to a falling portfolio. and failing health It's also the one asset that never comes back once it's gone.

If you've lost a lot of money and are dealing with a health matter, or any other personal setback, here's what's helping me. The number one goal is to hang on until the good times return.

Industry observers note that 1) Health is the real net worth. No amount of money makes you feel good when you're sick. If you're healthy right now, you're richer than you think, regardless of what your brokerage account indicates.

2) Measure your losses in time, not dollars. Losing a big chunk of your portfolio sounds catastrophic. But ask how far back the losses take you. Often you're only back to where you were a year or two ago during a correction or bear market. However, if you're sick of work, then a more conservative portfolio adjustment should be made.

In a recent development, 3) Don't make big decisions while you're sick or distraught. Selling everything at the bottom feels like relief in the moment. It's usually the most expensive relief you'll ever buy. Give yourself a cooling-off period before any major move. Leg out or into positions. No wholesale decisions.

4) Focus on what you can control. You can't control the Fed, AI spending, a CEO's escapades, or a virus. You can control your spending, your asset allocation, your sleep, and how you treat the people around you. Lean into spending time with people and things that bring you the most joy.

Industry observers note that 5) Do one thing that gets you outside your head. For me, it was taking the kids to Alcatraz and painting my downstairs hallway. For you, it might be a walk, a phone call with an old friend, or cooking a meal. Action beats rumination.

Industry observers note that 6) Write down your gratitude list. When your mind keeps spiraling toward worst-case scenarios, putting the good things in writing is a way to fight back.

Perhaps what I'm most thankful for is the opportunity to try again.

In a recent development, we've been through many corrections and bear markets before. None of them ever felt good. But over time, the stock market recovered, and we moved on with our lives.

In a recent development, the great thing about being at a low point is that there's likely more upside than downside. Yes, things can always get worse. But unless my illness turns fatal and the stock market falls more than 60%, forcing us to return to work, we'll be OK.

Sources indicate that finally, I can't talk well enough to record a podcast right now. But I can still move my fingers and write. So I'm thankful for the ability to keep going, no matter what.

Readers, what are you thankful for this year despite the market correction? Have you ever had to deal with a massive financial loss and a health setback at the same time, and how did you get through it? Do you find that losing money makes you more or less grateful for what you have? And what's one thing you plan to do this holiday season to get out of your own head?

If you want to build lasting wealth that can withstand corrections like this one, grab a copy of Millionaire Milestones: Simple Steps To Seven Figures, a USA Today bestseller from Portfolio Penguin. And if you're worried about your kids' future in an AI-driven world, keep an eye out for my upcoming book, Your Children Will Be OK.

Industry News: Huge Crowds Trek to Everest Base Camp

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the image of an endless line of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp this week seemed like deja vu.
  • Ngima Sherpa of Osprey Adventure explained that this is not the norm, but the delay caused by Cyclone Anwar, which hit Nepal last weekend, has created a huge backlog.
  • “Even though there are always a lot of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp, this kind of traffic is not usual,” Ngima Sherpa explained.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the image of an endless line of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp this week seemed like deja vu. Why are conga lines similar to the infamous ones filmed every May on Everest’s Hillary Step, now repeating at the base of the mountain? We asked the local trekking guide who shot the video.

Ngima Sherpa of Osprey Adventure explained that this is not the norm, but the delay caused by Cyclone Anwar, which hit Nepal last weekend, has created a huge backlog.

“Even though there are always a lot of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp, this kind of traffic is not usual,” Ngima Sherpa explained. “This video was shot on November 1, after three days of continuous snow and rain…During that time, all the trekkers were stuck in Dingboche, which is two trekking stages away from Everest Base Camp.”.

When the weather finally cleared, all those trekkers set off for EBC at the same time, causing heavy traffic on the route from Dingboche to Gorakshep.

The recent cyclone is also the reason why the surroundings are so heavily covered in snow. Usually, the entire trail to Everest Base Camp is dry.

The fresh snow on Nepal’s peaks is having consequences for those planning to summit trekking peaks. Conditions on otherwise straightforward snow slopes have become problematic, as climbers sink into deep, heavy snow.

Satori Adventures had to retreat after swimming in snow on the flanks of Mera Peak, in the Khumbu. “Four to five feet of fresh snow made it impossible to move forward above high camp,” leader Furba Sherpa reported.

According to recent reports, ramesh Gurung noted today that he has retreated from an attempt on 6,119m Lobuche East, another popular Khumbu 6000’er. However, Gurung said he will try again with another group soon.

Conditions will change only as the snow transforms under the dimming sun and freezes in the approaching winter temperatures.

On Ama Dablam, Sherpa climbers struggled to reopen the route to Camp 1 on Tuesday but managed to complete it. The route above Camp 1 follows a steep, mixed ridge with less accumulated snow. Several teams are now on their summit rotations and expect to top out in the next few days.

Tenzing Sherpa of Gokyo Namaste Lodge has shared some useful information for trekkers who strategy to cross the huge Ngozumpa Glacier between Gokyo and Dragnag. The recent snowfall makes the usual route less safe, and he recommends following local people along an easier route between Longbanga Tso (1st Lake) and Taujung Tso (2nd Lake). See Tenzing’s sketch of the route:.

Alternative route between Gokyo Lakes, suggested by Gokyo Tenzing Sherpa.

It has been revealed that tenzing also noted that the route from Thame to Gokyo is open, as the Gokyo Lodge Association cleared and reopened the trail from the Gokyo side yesterday. However, conditions on the glacier may change quickly.

The route across Gokyo is one of the most popular side trips in the Khumbu, for those wanting to enrich their Everest Base Camp trek. The area features stunning scenery, with high mountain lakes, glaciers, and a view of the formidable South Face of Cho Oyu.

#113891. Animal Attack Roundup, Nov. 4

📅 05 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (940 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

Animal Attack Roundup, Nov. 4

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (940 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that while they predominate the media reports, most animal attack victims are not tourists unwisely attempting to take selfies with wildlife.
  • It has been revealed that as expanding populations push human settlements further into wildlife habitat, we can expect to see more conflicts.
  • Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Tisha Mukherjee, CC BY-SA 4.0.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that while they predominate the media reports, most animal attack victims are not tourists unwisely attempting to take selfies with wildlife. People who live and work every day among animals are the ones who most often face the consequences.

It has been revealed that as expanding populations push human settlements further into wildlife habitat, we can expect to see more conflicts. Here are some recent incidents.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Tisha Mukherjee, CC BY-SA 4.0.

In a recent development, in Indonesia, 24-year-old Selviana Ambu Kaka was attacked by a crocodile while washing clothes in the Bondo Kodi River. Her fiancé and his sister witnessed a large crocodile emerging from the water, biting Ambu Kaka on the leg, and dragging her into the river. They immediately alerted nearby relatives and authorities, and a search commenced.

The people of Southwest Sumba, the closest town, organized and combed the area with nets. When they found a large crocodile matching witness descriptions, they hauled it onto shore and killed it. The animal measured nearly 4.9 meters long.

Early on the morning of October 24, Ambu Kaka’s remains were found approximately 30m from the attack site. She is one of many such victims in Indonesia, which sees more saltwater crocodile attacks than any other country.

Sources indicate that habitat destruction is largely behind the massive number of human-crocodile conflicts. It’s an understandably hard sell, however, for conservation workers to convince locals that preventing attacks means protecting the perpetrators.

The victim had recently returned from Jakarta to become formally engaged on October 30.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons/ Rohit Gangwal, CC BY-SA 4.0.

A 65-year-old farm laborer, Tulsi Rama Sawar, was killed by a leopard in state of Maharashtra, just north of Mumbai, on November 1. The noise of the attack summoned help from the locals. By the time they arrived, the leopard had fled, but Sawar was deceased. Her case comes less than a month after a leopard killed a 52-year-old woman in the same area.

Industry observers note that town residents are demanding immediate government action to capture the animal. If their demands for cage traps and cameras are not granted, locals threaten collective protest. The attacks represent a threat to their lives, but also their livelihoods, as farmers are unable to work the fields out of fear of attack.

In a recent development, elsewhere, in Uttar Pradesh near the Nepal border, a 45-year-old farmer named Kennu fought off an attacking leopard, sustaining serious injuries. The man was working in a sugarcane field when the predator leaped out from hiding. Kennu fought back, and the animal retreated long enough for him to flee home, where family members brought him to medical care. Forestry officials have urged agricultural workers to avoid working in the fields alone.

Farm workers are not the only leopard victims, however. Early in the morning of November 4, a 15-year-old girl was dragged from her home in the Shahdol district of central India.

Sources indicate that saraswati Singh Gond was sleeping in bed beside her sister on their veranda, which did not have a door. A leopard entered during the night, not even waking her sister. Singh Gond’s body was found approximately 300m from the house. The search for the leopard continues.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Shadow Ayush, CC BY-SA 4.0.

In a recent development, leopards are only one of the wildlife threats that rural Indians face. A 55-year-old woman was gathering mushrooms in Utterakand in northern India on October 30 when she was attacked and killed by a wild elephant. Devaki Rana was lifted up and thrown to the ground, her son reported.

The incident occurred in one of India’s elephant corridors, which allow highly endangered Asian elephant herds to move between their fragmented habitats. The corridors are essential to conservation, but also present a concentrated area where attacks are more common.

Another fatal encounter took place in the state of Chhattisgarh in east-central India. A man of between 35 and 40 years of age, traveling by motorcycle with his nephew, came upon an elephant standing in the road. It immediately charged them, killing the uncle, while his nephew managed to hide beneath a parked truck. Eventually, the elephant left, and he was able to escape.

In a recent development, locals believe that the elephant in question is one known as Kabra Kaan, which they see frequently and which has been connected with earlier incidents. The Forestry Department, however, has not confirmed this.

Elephant corridors allow them to pass between the remaining forested areas. Photo: Wildlife Trust of India.

It has been revealed that in Japan, brown bear attacks have been rising for several years. As in many places, human settlements are encroaching on brown bear territory. A decrease in farmland has left no boundary between the urban and the forested worlds. The government has responded with controversial bear culls, despite the concerns of conservation workers.

The latest incident is very different from the increasingly common attack stories. Late on the night of October 30, an express train running on Hokkaido’s Soya Line collided with a large brown bear. The body of the bear was trapped under the train, and the wheels derailed.

In a recent development, A brown bear became trapped beneath the wheels of Sarobetsu No 3. Photo: Hokkaido Railway Manufacturer.

Industry observers note that none of the crew or 32 passengers were injured in the crash. However, fearing more bears were in the area, officials kept everyone on the train overnight, until they could be safely extracted the following morning. Company officials have confirmed that this is the first bear-collision derailment in their nearly 40-year history.

Young Climbers Bag New Routes, Including First Ascent, in Rolwaling

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (702 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that an energetic foursome of young French climbers had a busy time recently in Nepal’s Rolwaling Valley, east of the Khumbu.
  • It has been revealed that as soon as the climbers reached Rolwaling, they had to change their primary goal, which was in poor condition.
  • “Before long, the climbing turned vertical, and the ridge became razor-sharp and exposed,” Bazon wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that an energetic foursome of young French climbers had a busy time recently in Nepal’s Rolwaling Valley, east of the Khumbu. Eric Bazon, Pierre Girot, Sophie Jacob, and Kilian Moni did two upcoming routes, including a first ascent of a 5,205m rocky spire and one very difficult line. They then climbed another peak on a “rest” day.

It has been revealed that as soon as the climbers reached Rolwaling, they had to change their primary goal, which was in poor condition. Their acclimatization was also progressing more slowly than expected. Instead, they focused their attention on a ridge they saw from their base camp every morning. On October 20, Bazon, Jacob, and Girot set off toward the summit, while Moni waited for them at the base.

“Before long, the climbing turned vertical, and the ridge became razor-sharp and exposed,” Bazon wrote. The climb took three days on the ridge, bivvies included, and led Bazon, Sophie Jacob, and Pierre Girot to the west summit of ChekiGo (6,128m). It took another full day and one more bivouac to reach base camp.

It has been revealed that cheki Go’s main summit was first climbed in 2005 by Bruce Normand of the UK and Oliver Von Rotz of Switzerland via the west face. A Spanish team led by Mikel Zabalza first reached the west summit via a direct route up the west face in 2017. The team had just returned from bagging the first ascent of Jugal II.

“It was quite an intense experience for a ‘secondary’ project: one that combined rock climbing on mediocre granite, improvised protection, and steep snow ridges, all while hauling our ropes on our backs,” mentioned Bazon.

It has been revealed that the ridge was technical enough to be a good start: 5c on rock and M4 on mixed terrain. In Alpine grades, the team assessed it as TD (very difficult).

The ridge on ChekiGo. Photo: Eric Bazon.

Since the weather forecast looked good for another four days, the team decided to continue climbing. They split into two teams: Bazon and Girot headed for a peak previously climbed by elite American alpinists Domen Kastelic and Sam Hennessey in 2014: Chukyima Go (6,259m). Like their predecessors, the French team approached the west face from the Naa Valley in Rolwaling.

“There was this direct, narrow, and obvious couloir that simply begged to be climbed,” Bazon reported.

According to recent reports, the climbers at an open bivy. Photo: Eric Bazon.

The next morning, they found the west face in great condition, which allowed them to climb a direct route to the summit along rock cracks, steep ice, and varied mixed terrain.

It took them two days (October 27-28), with one cold bivy on the face with their feet in their backpacks, to complete the route’s 23 pitches. Their West Face Direct route is 900m long, and the team assessed it as ED (extremely difficult), with M6 on mixed sections, and an Alpine ice grade of AI5.

The photo below highlights that the fresh French route, TchikitaMa Go, runs to the right of the previous line opened by the two Americans.

It has been revealed that left: the new route opened by the French team, compared, right, to the 2014 line by Domen Kastelic and Sam Hennessey. Photo: Eric Bazon/PlanetMountain.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, Sophie Jacob and Kilian Moni went for an unclimbed peak that also rose right in front of their base camp: 5,205m Janjmu. The pair completed the first ascent on an aesthetic 600m line up the north face. They called the route The Eternal Stars (“Les etoiles eternelles”) after some friends who had recently perished.

“It felt just like being at home in the Alps, with the added challenge of high altitude,” the climbers reported. “We pushed ourselves to the limit, both physically and mentally, across demanding yet incredibly logical pitches.”.

But this was still not enough for the pair. They squeezed in a final climb of Yalung Ri in what they called “a contemplative, active recovery” day. They then finished the trip by paragliding from the summit.

Recent findings suggest that kilian Moni flies from the top of Yalung Ri. Photo: Kilian Moni.

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (611 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

Duo Completes Baffin Island Circuit By Skiing, Hiking, and Packrafting

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Caleb McDaniels, 25, and Henry Penfold, 22, have completed their impressive expedition around Baffin Island.
  • According to recent reports, the pair began and ended in Iqaluit, Nunavut’s capital.
  • The pair’s completed route around Baffin Island.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Caleb McDaniels, 25, and Henry Penfold, 22, have completed their impressive expedition around Baffin Island. The Americans combined skiing, hiking, and packrafting to almost circle the world’s fifth-largest island. McDaniels told ExplorersWeb they did about 20% skiing and the rest was evenly split between backpacking and packrafting.

According to recent reports, the pair began and ended in Iqaluit, Nunavut’s capital. The final section of their trip was also the longest, a 1,130km stretch with no villages after Igloolik to resupply. They made light work of it, knocking it out in 40 days and bringing their total distance to 3,262km over 145 days, from their late May start to their return to Iqaluit in mid-October. By then, the oncoming Arctic winter gave them few hours of light to work with.

The pair’s completed route around Baffin Island. Photo: Caleb McDaniels.

Industry observers note that with no resupply points, the pair left Igloolik with 82kg of food. They hoped to do it in seven weeks but brought even more food, because they weren’t sure how long that giant giant section would actually take, explained Caleb McDaniels.

“With no way to carry that much weight in our packs, we loaded up our packrafts and paddled the first 400 miles [644km]. Then, for the final 300 miles [483km], we heaved on our packs to walk overland,” they explained.

According to recent reports, the paddling portion went quickly, aided by some ingenuity. “Much of the time, we were able to sail using our trekking poles as masts and panels cut out of an old tent for sails. Speeding along at over five mph, we did some incredible downwinding, spray flying from our bows.”.

It has been revealed that using makeshift sails. Photo: Caleb McDaniels.

Postholing through early winter snow back to Iqaluit. Photo: Caleb McDaniels.

“It was more of a postholing session — we slowly picked our way across snow-covered boulder fields and partly frozen marshlands. Constantly breaking through thin ice over the tundra marshes, we walked in our drysuits to keep our legs and feet dry. Each morning required half an hour of chipping ice and melting out our shoes, which invariably froze solid,” they said.

Sources indicate that mcDaniels and Penfold had planned a roughly circular route around the island, but “we weren’t trying to circumnavigate Baffin,” McDaniels told ExplorersWeb. Two previous parties had circumnavigated the island by dogteam, but McDaniels and Penfold’s route was driven by aesthetic considerations rather than to satisfy a catchy trip definition.

Slogging overland. Photo: Caleb McDaniels.

They chose their route after looking at satellite images and enjoyed both spectacular scenery and some special wildlife sightings, including at least one that was a little too close for comfort.

Recent findings suggest that “One morning, as I went to fill our water bottles, I stumbled upon a sleeping polar bear hidden behind a low rise. Only a few yards away, it lifted its massive white head and glared at me for a moment before returning to its nap in the sun,” McDaniels wrote. “I carefully retreated behind the rise and yelled over to Henry to get the shotgun and flares out just in case. We quickly packed our boats and got on the water.”.

Industry observers note that in Foxe Basin, they almost collided with a sleeping walrus, and on Nettilling Lake, they met one of the resident seals. “He was immensely curious and not at all afraid. He swam around our boats for half an hour, playing with our stern lines and swimming back and forth between us. At one point, I put my hand into the water, and he brushed it with his nose!”.

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

Americans Bag Major First Ascent in Pakistan

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (964 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that americans Dane Steadman and Cody Winckler, awarded with a Piolet d’Or in 2025 after the first ascent of Yashkuk Sar, have done a similar monster 1,800m-long fresh route on the north face of Sosbun Brakk (6,414m).
  • This first ascent of the peak’s north face included difficulties up to M7, WI5.
  • Meanwhile, the airline misplaced Winckler’s baggage — every adventurer’s nightmare.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that americans Dane Steadman and Cody Winckler, awarded with a Piolet d’Or in 2025 after the first ascent of Yashkuk Sar, have done a similar monster 1,800m-long fresh route on the north face of Sosbun Brakk (6,414m). This time, Grant Stewart joined them for this off-season climb in the Karakoram.

This first ascent of the peak’s north face included difficulties up to M7, WI5. The climbers had to overcome several obstacles before even setting foot on the face. Like many other alpine-style teams this season, they were originally planning to climb another peak. But instead of adapting because of washed-out trails, they had bureaucratic challenges. Their permit, obtained 10 months earlier, was revoked some weeks before their departure. They had to promptly find a different goal.

Meanwhile, the airline misplaced Winckler’s baggage — every adventurer’s nightmare. Somehow, the outfitter sent it to base camp some days later. Then, Steadman had to overcome serious Acute Mountain Sickness in base camp. Their acclimatization was hampered by freak spells of bad weather. Finally, the line on Sosbun Brakk they initially chose was too hard and risky because of a hanging serac they only spotted after they began.

The team’s lonely base camp. Photo: Dane Steadman.

“Back at BC, it was time to rest, regroup, and contemplate a totally different line that we’d seen from on the wall, which gave us new hope,” Steadman recalled.

According to recent reports, off to the north face. Photo: Dane Steadman.

On October 1, the three climbers set off on that potential new line. “Instead of angling left up hard mixed ground above the cone as before, we made an arcing traverse right, across an ice apron, to gain runnels on the right side of the face,” Steadman explained.

The team gained 800m on that first day and set their first bivouac on a snowy arete, just in time to be slammed by a violent storm that kept them in their tent the whole next day.

It has been revealed that steep mixed terrain. Photo: Dane Steadman.

It has been revealed that A tarp to protect the team’s bivouac from falling spindrift. Photo: Dane Steadman.

“In the morning, we made a gamble for the top by leaving the tent and starting up a massive gully system,” Steward wrote. “At its top, we reached another dead end in a huge serac barrier. To escape this, Dane committed to a visionary pitch, casting off up a blank slab to eventually reach an ice smear.”.

Chaotic, difficult rocky sections. Photo: Dane Steadman.

“A huge serac to our right and smooth slabs out left posed a serious question; eight meters of sideways teetering on tiny gneissic edges and a miraculous rock thread were the answer,” stated Steadman.

It has been revealed that “We continued up the massive hanging glacier to reach the hallucinatory final headwall of steep ice/mixed climbing and mushroom-weaving lunacy,” Stewart continued. “One final traverse with 1,800m of exposure under our feet and a magically appearing, dead-vertical ice tongue led us to the summit ridge.”.

Industry observers note that A totally vertical section. Photo: Grant Stewart.

“The wild terrain on the upper mountain took longer than we wanted,” Steadman admitted. By the time they finally reached the summit, it was 4 pm, the storm was coming the following day, and they still had a long way (and many rappels) down.

Summit picture on Sosbun Brakk. Left to right, Dane Steadman, Grant Stewart, and Cody Wrincker. Photo: Dane Steadman.

“The sun would set around 6 pm, so we threaded the first of 35 rappels and started down. Long after dark, we finally arrived back at our bivy ledge at around 5,800m,” Steadman recalled.

The storm was not supposed to start until noon the following day, but it was already snowing at 8 am, with still 1,200 vertical meters of descent to go.

It has been revealed that rappelling down the route. Photo: Dane Steadman.

“Before long, we were caught in a proper storm,” Stewart explained. “We committed to a faster and hopefully safer descent by rappelling down the west rib to the Sokha/Sosbun col. By the time we reached the col, we could barely communicate over the screaming southwest wind.”.

Sources indicate that after some scary rappels in high winds down the serac band, the climbers finally reached a sheltered section of the face. They still had to deal with heavy spindrift coming from above until finally, at around 4 pm, they touched down on the glacier. And yet, the adventure was not over — especially for Grant Stewart:.

In a recent development, following Dane, I took maybe 10 steps when I felt the ground under me crack. Instinctively, I jumped and landed on my stomach as a huge crevasse swallowed the ground behind me. Soaking wet, we began postholing into the wan light of a mesmerizing white out.

[We stuck] to the center of the glacier as avalanches rumbled down all around in the whirling snow. After a strange eternity, the ragged colors of a tent appeared and we were greeted by ecstatic dancing, big hugs, and endless cups of chai from (our BC crew) Ibrahim and Idrees.

Recent findings suggest that happy climbers and base camp crew after a safe return from the summit. Photo: Dane Steadman.

In a recent development, the team didn’t report their success and the details of the climb until they returned home. And then, the first words of appraisal were not for the route itself, but for the mountains and people of Gilgit-Baltistan.

“It’s a unique place…where continents and cultures collide. Trips there, while often difficult, are rewarding in ways hard to describe simply,” Steadman stated. This was his third trip to the Karakoram, a place he has fallen in love with.

Industry News: Weekend Warm-Up: Assynt

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (394 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Explorersweb

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Assynt, subtitled “Home is where the croft is,” is a short documentary that brings viewers to the Scottish Highland community of Assynt, where residents live on traditional crofts.
  • The croft is a uniquely Scottish term, describing the smaller, less fertile plots of land that poorer people were forced onto, following the infamous Highland Clearances of the 18th and 19th centuries.
  • It has been revealed that it was a very hard life.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Assynt, subtitled “Home is where the croft is,” is a short documentary that brings viewers to the Scottish Highland community of Assynt, where residents live on traditional crofts.

The croft is a uniquely Scottish term, describing the smaller, less fertile plots of land that poorer people were forced onto, following the infamous Highland Clearances of the 18th and 19th centuries. Crofters lived on their crofts and farmed for subsistence, grazing sheep on shared land. Unable to support themselves on the croft alone, most also worked in fishing, kelp, or peat to support themselves.

It has been revealed that it was a very hard life. But Lewis MacAskill, whom the viewer is soon introduced to, doesn’t see it that way. He is one of just over a thousand residents of Assynt, who chose to stay and continue the crofting tradition.

“I regard the croft as an extension of who I am as a person,” MacAskill explains.

In a recent development, the small community of Assynt. Photo: Screenshot.

It has been revealed that macAskill introduces us to some of the other members of the community. Anna is a sheepdog owner and trainer, whom we see herding sheep using the same techniques people here have used for centuries. Stuart is a passionate fisherman, who shares his love of Assynt’s natural landscape with his young son.

Sources indicate that we also meet some of the creatives who have, MacAskill indicates, been drawn by the unique landscape and material culture. We see a potter using local materials, a fiddler, and a spinner on her spinning wheel.

Recent findings suggest that the spinning wheel came to Europe from the Middle East by the 13th century, and was widely adopted by the 18th century, replacing the older drop spindle and distaff. Photo: Screenshot.

MacAskill moved to the croft a decade ago, and doesn’t regret it. Having grown up visiting every summer, he has always felt drawn to the land and knows others feel the same. But a small, isolated community like Assynt is constantly in danger of depopulation. MacAskill hopes that people keep choosing to move back and stay, heeding the same call he did.

The film ends on this note, with a montage of scenes from life in Assynt and the landscape it sits in, while an elderly crofter sings a traditional Scottish song of homecoming.
